title: Knowledge check: Query Strings and URL Parameters

questions.prompt: Which subtopic is explicitly listed under “Query Strings and URL Parameters” in the attached Classic ASP curriculum?
questions.explanation: The PDF lists “Understanding URL parameters” under lesson 42, “Query Strings and URL Parameters”. The distractors belong to other lesson topics.

questions.prompt: When applying “Query Strings and URL Parameters” in a legacy Classic ASP application, which approach is strongest?
options: Return the full connection string to the browser when debugging.
Keep every Recordset open for the whole session.
Validate input, bind values as ADO parameters, and close database resources reliably.
Concatenate user values directly into SQL.
questions.answer_key: Validate input, bind values as ADO parameters, and close database resources reliably.
questions.explanation: This approach keeps query strings and url parameters testable and respects Classic ASP/IIS runtime boundaries. The exact IIS, provider, or component behavior must be checked in the target test environment.

questions.prompt: Before marking work on “Query Strings and URL Parameters” ready for review, what evidence should be recorded?
options: Treat a successful happy-path test as proof of all security properties.
Document the observed result, tool/runtime version, and one meaningful failure or edge case.
Claim the production deployment passed without running it.
Delete diagnostic evidence before recording the outcome.
questions.answer_key: Document the observed result, tool/runtime version, and one meaningful failure or edge case.
questions.explanation: Good maintenance evidence includes the expected and observed result, relevant version/runtime assumptions, and a boundary or failure test. Never claim an execution/deployment test that was not run.
